attributes.body:
あまり is a very flexible word in Japanese, that is used in several different grammar points. When paired with the ない form of a word, it translates to 'not very (A)', or 'hardly (A)'. To pair あまり (or the casual form, あんまり) with another word, we just need to place it at the beginning of a phrase, or directly before the ない statement.

Fun Fact

Although あまり～ない is regularly translated as 'not very' the literal translation is closer to 'not excessively (A)'. This is due to 余（あま）り (the kanji which this word comes from), meaning 'excessive', or 'to be in excess'.

あまり has this meaning of 'excessive' in all of its grammar points, and the nuance will only change based on whether the sentence itself is positive (does not use ない), or negative (uses ない).

Both 別に〜ない and あまり〜ない are used to qualify negative statements, but differ in nuance. あまり〜ない expresses a lesser degree, e.g. あまり痛くない ('It doesn't hurt much.'). In contrast, 別に〜ない adds a tone of indifference or dismissal, e.g. 別に痛くない ('It's not like it hurts.', implying that there is no need to worry, etc.).

attributes.body: あまり has the base meaning of 'excess', but its nuance changes with context. Together with a negative word in the form あまり～ない, it means 'not very (A)', e.g. あまり寒くない ('It's not very cold.'). Used affirmatively, it implies something of an excessive degree, e.g. 緊張のあまりうまくできなかった ('I was so nervous I couldn't do it well.').

attributes.body: たくさん is a noun meaning 'many' or 'a lot,' often used with verbs (e.g. たくさん食べた = 'I ate a lot'). To express the opposite idea ('not much' or 'not many'), the pattern あまり～ない is used (e.g. あまり食べなかった = 'I didn't eat much'). Note that あまり originally means 'excess' and can also appear in affirmative forms (see あまりに).

attributes.body: Both あまり～ない and そんなに express a negative degree, but with different nuance. あまり～ない means 'not very' in a general sense, e.g. あまり寒くない ('It's not very cold.'). そんなに (literally 'that much') can imply comparison to a standard and can be used with both negative and affirmative phrases, e.g. そんなに好きなら 'if you like [it] that much...' and そんなに好きじゃない ('I don't like it that much.').
